title: Predictive slot-packing and cost-signal tuning for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build a predictive slot-packing engine and accompanying autoscale policy tuning workflow that reduces committed-capacity waste while preserving throughput SLAs for Dedicated pools. Background: customers frequently over-provision to avoid throttles during burst windows; current heuristics are reactive (scale-up on pressure) and produce either high cost or risk of SLO breaches. This ticket scopes a combined approach: (1) a lightweight demand predictor that infers per-tenant expected qps/seq-length distributions from 14-day patterns and schedule signals, (2) a slot-packing optimizer that maps predicted demand into slot/instance reservations with headroom bands, and (3) a cost-signal tuning step that proposes autoscale policy parameters (scale thresholds, cooldowns, burst allocations) per-pool. Goals: reduce average committed GPU hours by >= 12% across pilot pools while keeping p99 latency regression <= 5% and throughput loss < 0.5%. Success looks like a generated sizing recommendation for each pool, an automated policy suggestion visible in Console, and a 2-week canary showing cost reduction without customer incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive model produces a 7-day ahead qps forecast with median MAPE <= 12% on historical pools
Slot-packing optimizer yields per-pool recommendations that reduce committed hours by >= 12% on pilot dataset
Autoscale policy suggester emits parameters (min_slots, max_slots, scale_up_threshold, scale_down_threshold, cooldown_ms) and maps to Console UI without manual translation
Rollout plan and safety nets implemented: canary to 10% of pools, automatic fallback to previous commit on SLO alert
End-to-end dashboards (utilization, projected vs. actual cost savings, SLO deltas) available in Console and surfaced to Eng and PM teams
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after Fleet Ops review; initial scoping meeting with PM/Infra/Console teams. Agreed target savings and safety constraints.

2025-02-18: Data availability check complete. Raw telemetry (slot-level utilization, tenant qps, seq length histograms) available in bigtable + daily rollups. Need additional enrichment for schedule signals (cron/traffic tags).
2025-02-24: PoC predictive model (lightgbm) trained on 30 pools; median MAPE 14% — close but misses weekend-heavy tenants. Decided to add weekday/weekend embedding and schedule features.

2025-03-01: Slot-packing optimizer prototype (ILP-based) returns reasonable mappings but is slow at fleet scale (~45s/pool). Switching to greedy-first-fit with iterative balancing for production performance.

2025-03-03: UX spike with Console team; identified required UI fields for policy suggestions and rollback button. Drafted API contract for suggestions endpoint: /v1/dedicated/pools/:id/suggest-sizing.

2025-03-05: Integration plan approved in Architecture sync. Decided to run a 4-week simulation backtest before canary. Assigned Marco to lead infra integration and Aisha to own model tuning. Next: build simulation harness and dashboard mocks.
notes: Trade-offs: ILP gives optimal packing but is computationally expensive; greedy heuristic with rebalancing expected to hit 95% of optimal with 10x lower runtime. Safety-first rollout: predictions map to suggested min_slots only; existing autoscale rules remain in effect until canary completes. Will coordinate with CSM for customers on Dedicated plans before canary activation.
implementation_plan: 1) Data prep and feature engineering (2 weeks), 2) Model + simulator (3 weeks), 3) Optimizer + API + Console integration (2 weeks), 4) Backtest and canary (4 weeks), 5) Post-canary adjustments and wide rollout.
postmortem_plan: If canary SLOs degrade > 5% p99 or any customer reports SLA violations, immediately revert suggestions, whitelist affected pools, and run root-cause within 24 hours. Collect telemetry and update model/optimizer constraints.
communication: Will publish weekly progress to #fleet-efficiency; hold demo for Platform PMs and Solutions Engineering before canary. Prepare customer-facing FAQ for CSMs explaining suggested sizing and safety nets.
